content.description: A Graphic Designer creates visual assets — logos, brand identity systems, marketing collateral, packaging, social media graphics, and print/digital layouts — that communicate a message or brand clearly and attractively. They work primarily in tools like Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, and InDesign, translating a client's or marketing team's brief into finished visual output, and typically collaborate with marketing, content, and sometimes product teams. Unlike a UI/UX Designer, who focuses on interactive digital product interfaces, user flows, and usability testing, a Graphic Designer more often works on static or campaign-based visual output for branding, advertising, and print. Unlike an Illustrator, who creates original artwork from scratch, a Graphic Designer more often composes and arranges existing visual elements (photography, typography, icons, brand assets) into a cohesive layout.

vnMarket.value: Thị trường thiết kế đồ họa tại Việt Nam đang mở rộng nhờ ba động lực chính: sự bùng nổ thương mại điện tử trên Shopee, TikTok Shop, Lazada khiến doanh nghiệp cần lượng lớn banner, ảnh sản phẩm và video ngắn mỗi tháng; xu hướng xây dựng thương hiệu cá nhân và doanh nghiệp trên mạng xã hội đòi hỏi nội dung hình ảnh chuyên nghiệp, nhất quán; và làn sóng chuyển đổi số khiến cả startup công nghệ và doanh nghiệp truyền thống đều cần thiết kế UI/UX cho website và ứng dụng di động. Nhu cầu nhân lực trải rộng trên nhiều mảng: nhận diện thương hiệu, UI/UX, quảng cáo, in ấn, bao bì, game, hoạt hình.

salary.value: Theo Indeed (312 mức lương được báo cáo trong 36 tháng qua, cập nhật 6/9/2026), mức lương trung bình của Graphic Designer tại Việt Nam khoảng 12,37 triệu VNĐ/tháng, dao động từ 7,82 đến 19,56 triệu VNĐ/tháng.

demand.value: Theo CareerLink, nhu cầu tuyển dụng ngành Thiết kế đồ họa tại Việt Nam tăng khoảng 15-20% mỗi năm trong giai đoạn 2024-2026, cao hơn tốc độ tăng trưởng toàn cầu của ngành (dự kiến khoảng 3% trong giai đoạn 2023-2033), do quá trình chuyển đổi số diễn ra nhanh.

similarJobs.name: UI/UX Designer
similarJobs.distinction: Focuses on interface usability, user flows, and interaction/wireframe testing for digital products, rather than static or print visual assets.

similarJobs.name: Motion Graphic Designer
similarJobs.distinction: Specializes in animated graphics and video-based visual content rather than static layouts and print/digital collateral.

similarJobs.name: Illustrator
similarJobs.distinction: Creates original hand-drawn or digitally illustrated artwork from scratch, rather than composing layouts from existing visual elements like a Graphic Designer.

similarJobs.name: Art Director
similarJobs.distinction: Oversees the creative vision and output of a design team across projects, rather than personally executing individual design deliverables.

hardSkills.name: Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign)
hardSkills.description: The industry-standard toolset for producing, editing, and laying out professional graphic design work in Vietnam.

hardSkills.name: Typography & layout principles
hardSkills.description: Choosing and arranging type and visual hierarchy correctly is fundamental to legible, effective design across all formats.

hardSkills.name: Brand identity & logo design
hardSkills.description: Many roles require building or extending a consistent visual identity system across multiple brand touchpoints.

hardSkills.name: Print & packaging production knowledge
hardSkills.description: Understanding color modes, bleed, resolution, and print specifications is necessary for work that goes to physical production.

hardSkills.name: Basic motion graphics (After Effects)
hardSkills.description: Increasing demand for short-form video content on social platforms makes basic animation skills a valuable addition to static design.

hardSkills.name: UI design basics (Figma)
hardSkills.description: Many Graphic Designer roles in Vietnam now overlap with simple digital/UI layout work, especially at smaller companies without a dedicated UI/UX hire.

softSkills.name: Creativity & visual storytelling
softSkills.description: Translating a brand message or campaign idea into a compelling visual is the core value a designer brings.

softSkills.name: Attention to detail
softSkills.description: Alignment, spacing, and color consistency errors are highly visible in finished design work.

softSkills.name: Receptiveness to feedback
softSkills.description: Design work goes through multiple client or stakeholder review rounds, requiring the ability to revise without losing quality or motivation.

softSkills.name: Time management
softSkills.description: Designers typically juggle several concurrent briefs with overlapping deadlines.

softSkills.name: Client/stakeholder communication
softSkills.description: Explaining and defending design decisions to marketing teams or clients is a routine part of the job.
